The interaction between Epiquinamide and Isopentenyl-diphosphate Delta-isomerase is inferred through the cascade of targets, where the inhibition of UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 2B15 by Euphoscopin A could lead to the direct or indirect inhibition of Isopentenyl-diphosphate Delta-isomerase. This suggests that Epiquinamide may act through a multi-step mechanism involving the modulation of UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 2B15, which in turn affects the activity of Isopentenyl-diphosphate Delta-isomerase. The evidence supports a plausible mechanistic pathway, though further experimental validation is needed to confirm the direct interaction between Epiquinamide and Isopentenyl-diphosphate Delta-isomerase.
